correctness.rationale: The published Theorem B and Proposition 41 yield the exhaustive two-cycle dichotomy for b >= 10. On each finite sign-itinerary cell, the map is Mz+u+bv with integer M,u,v; if M=0, irrational b prevents its constant image from being a point whose first coordinate has b coefficient +/-1/3. Thus each exceptional inverse image lies in finitely many lines, giving planar nullity and dimension at most one. An explicit ray in the first quadrant maps to the exceptional cycle, giving dimension exactly one. Rank-zero cells hitting the good cycle give an open dense full-measure core. The checker verifies finite algebra only; no experimental extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: The cited source explicitly asks whether plateau asymptotic behavior extends to an open dense/full-Lebesgue-measure set in the ambient plane. This proof supplies both assertions on a natural uncountable and full-parameter-measure half-line of irrational b, and additionally determines exact Hausdorff dimension 1 of the exceptional stable basin. The dimension distinguishes genuinely thin exceptions from simply zero-area sets and explains arithmetic genericity.
